Elon Musk reveals how Starlink saved Ukraine from collapse, and sets the record straight on claims he throttled it:

“There is no private individual who has helped Ukraine more than I have. I made sure that Starlink was in Ukraine, prepositioned ahead of the Russian invasion.”

“When Russia invaded, they disabled all communications, all cell towers, all fiber cables, and every satellite communication system. There was one system they could not disable, and that was Starlink.”

“If they had not had Starlink, their entire line would have collapsed because they had no communication system, and Russia would have won. Now, does that sound like a pro-Russian action to you?”

“Even to this present day, Starlink provides the backbone of communications for the Ukrainian military and for Ukraine more broadly. If we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately.”

“From the beginning, I said that Starlink is a civilian system. It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government.”

“In the Starlink system, there is a speed limit. That speed limit is the speed of the fastest road speed limit in Ukraine, which I think is about 80 miles an hour.”

“Do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives, not just soldiers. That is not my position to do. And yet we’ve been pressed relentlessly to do that, which I think is outrageous.”

“Those are the rules that have been in place since the beginning, for years. Now people pressure me to change it, but I’m not changing it.”

quoted.text:
Elon Musk on why the historic Starship catch is a much bigger milestone than most people realize

“Catching the ship was the final major piece”

SpaceX has now achieved:

• 3 successful Super Heavy booster catches
• A booster that was reflown and caught again
• The FIRST EVER Starship upper-stage catch
• Ship 42 returning from orbit in good enough condition to be reflown with only minor repairs

For the first time, SpaceX has demonstrated that both stages of Starship can return and be recovered by the launch tower

And Elon confirmed that Ship 42 will likely be preserved for public display because of its historic achievement

“No one has ever taken a stage like that and created a truly reusable upper stage and certainly not brought it back to land propulsively while being caught by giant chopsticks”

Now look at what full and rapid reusability is expected to unlock:

• Up to 100 TIMES lower cost of accessing space
• The potential to deliver MILLIONS OF TONS of payload to orbit annually
• A transportation system where both stages return, refuel, and fly again

That's the scale of what SpaceX is building

Starship has already demonstrated the recovery of both stages. The next step is turning recovery into routine, rapid reuse

And that's what will fundamentally change the economics of spaceflight

quoted.text:
Elon Musk just shared an ambitious timeline for Terafab, which is being designed to become the largest building on Earth at 100 million square feet

And the first test chip is targeted for June 2027

"Terafab is still in its infancy, obviously. We only announced it earlier this year, but we've already recruited quite a strong team, and we're looking for more great engineers to join the Terafab project. It is one of the most exciting projects in the world: to create the largest, most advanced chip fabrication facility on Earth. In fact, it'll be the largest building of any kind on Earth. We expect it to ultimately be 100 million square feet, densely packed with the most advanced equipment in the world

We'll use relatively standard equipment at first, but then we'll be pushing suppliers to do special versions of the machines. In some cases, we may make our own machine if we feel that has to be done in order to improve the production process

So yes, I think it's going quite well. We expect to have the research fab in operation and hopefully make our first test chip around June of next year. So I guess we're about eight or nine months away from that. And if all goes well, we will achieve volume production towards the end of 2028, at least for phase one of Terafab. And then we'll go to phase two and onwards. But I think you'll see some very rapid evolution in the way that chips are made"
